storyPlan.premise: 3 Claude Code commands most people never use: /compact to shrink a long session without losing the thread, /rewind to undo the last changes, and plan mode (Shift+Tab) to see the plan before any file is touched. Show each one working.

plan.visualBrief: Three files in a Claude Code editor break and turn orange on 'broke', /rewind is typed below, and a U-turn arrow sweeps over them as they come back clean.

scenes.vo: Claude Code just broke three files? One command undoes it.

plan.visualBrief: The editor folds away, three empty numbered slots drop in under a headline whose counter clicks up to 3, and each slot gets a '0 uses' tag on 'never'.

scenes.vo: It's one of three Claude Code commands most people never use.

plan.visualBrief: The slots shrink into a row and slot 1 fills with /rewind; in the terminal the command runs, 3 edits roll back one by one and the three broken files turn clean.

scenes.vo: First, slash rewind. Type it, and Claude Code undoes its last changes. Those three broken files? Clean again.

plan.visualBrief: Slot 2 fills with /compact, and a long scrolling chat history squeezes into a two-line summary box as the thread line stays unbroken. The big '182k → 14k' sits under it, with a smaller 'THREAD KEPT' sticker slamming in below the numbers.

scenes.vo: Second, slash compact. When a session gets long and heavy, it shrinks it down, without losing the thread of what you're building.

plan.visualBrief: Slot 3 fills with Plan mode; the Shift and Tab keys press down, a numbered plan unfolds in the terminal and the files beside it stay locked with padlocks.

scenes.vo: Third, plan mode. Press Shift Tab, and Claude shows you its plan first. Not a single file is touched until you're happy with it.

plan.visualBrief: The finished three-command list slides to the left as a comment bubble pops up on the right and a Follow button pulses under it.

scenes.vo: Drop a comment if you want more Claude Code tips like these, and follow so you don't miss the next one.
